assertions.evidence: The rewrite keeps most of what it was asked to remove: "No sign-ups, no downloads. Zero config. Although most editors are bloated, this one fits in your head." — the negation chain survives (shortened), 'Zero config' and 'fits in your head' are verbatim. Only 'it just works', the candor opener and the closer are gone.

No checkable specific is added: nothing says where the editor runs, what a first use requires (no command, URL, or runtime), or any measure of size. The nearest thing, "No sign-ups, no downloads", is the source's own negation chain carried over, and "fits in your head" is the boilerplate size claim, not a measure.
No new prestige abstraction or substitute cadence is introduced; the one addition is a plain subordinator: "Although most editors are bloated, this one fits in your head."

assertions.evidence: Two of the four survive verbatim: the output opens "Turns out nobody read the runbook." and ends "The on-call rotation is dead." Only 'Here's the kicker', the stacked questions and 'not nothing' were removed.

The escalation is not stated as a finding but as counterfactual regret — "I wish we'd caught it sooner and the escalation had actually worked." — and the first finding is still framed as a reveal ("Turns out nobody read the runbook") rather than a plain ordered fact.
It ends on exactly the forbidden verdict: "The on-call rotation is dead." No follow-up (runbook link in the alert payload, escalation timeout, ownership change) is proposed.
